<thought>The 1H NMR shows a single aromatic signal integrating to 10 H at 7.51 ppm, which is characteristic of a highly symmetric aromatic hydrocarbon containing ten equivalent protons. The simplest structure matching this description is biphenyl (C₁₂H₁₀). Its aromatic protons appear around 7.5 ppm and, due to the symmetry of the two phenyl rings, can be reported as a single combined signal. Therefore, the most plausible SMILES for the unknown sample is “c1ccccc1-c2ccccc2”.</thought>
<final_answer>c1ccccc1-c2ccccc2</final_answer>
